meta.titre: Types of Chemical Reactions: recognising the pattern

sections.contenu_markdown: In a school laboratory in Kumba, a student drops a strip of zinc into blue copper sulphate and watches the colour fade, then neutralises acid with alkali, then burns a candle. These look like completely different events, yet chemists place them into a small number of types. Recognising the type of a reaction lets you predict the products, write the equation and describe what you will see, even for a reaction you have never met. The GCE O/L paper regularly asks you to name a type of reaction, give a definition and an equation with an example, and to identify the type from an equation.

items: Chemical formulae of common acids, bases and salts, and how to balance a simple equation.
A compound can be an acid, a base, an alkali or a salt.
Alkenes such as ethene contain a carbon-carbon double bond, and alkanes such as methane contain only single bonds.

sections.titre: Classifying chemical reactions by their pattern
sections.contenu_markdown:
Ask first: **how many reactants and products are there, and what kind of substances are they?**

| Type | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Combination (synthesis) | two or more substances form one product | $2\mathrm{Na} + \mathrm{Cl_{2}} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ |
| Decomposition | one compound gives two or more simpler substances (by heat, electricity or light) | $2\mathrm{H_{2}O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{H_{2}} + \mathrm{O_{2}}$ (electrolysis); heating is *thermal* decomposition |
| Displacement | a more reactive element replaces a less reactive one in a compound | $\mathrm{Zn} + \mathrm{CuSO_{4}} \rightarrow \mathrm{ZnSO_{4}} + \mathrm{Cu}$ |
| Double decomposition (precipitation) | two solutions swap partners and an insoluble solid forms | $\mathrm{AgNO_{3}} + \mathrm{NaCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{AgCl} + \mathrm{NaNO_{3}}$ |
| Neutralisation | acid + base (or alkali) gives salt + water | $\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaCl} + \mathrm{H_{2}O}$ |
| Combustion | a substance burns in oxygen and gives out heat | $\mathrm{CH_{4}} + 2\mathrm{O_{2}} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO_{2}} + 2\mathrm{H_{2}O}$ |

Two more terms are not exclusive types but describe the electrons:

- **Redox:** any reaction in which electrons are transferred (combination of a metal with a non-metal and displacement are redox).
- **Exothermic or endothermic:** the reaction gives out heat (combustion, neutralisation) or takes in heat (thermal decomposition).

A reaction can fit more than one description. For example, $2\mathrm{Mg} + \mathrm{O_{2}} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MgO}$ is a combination, a combustion and a redox reaction at the same time. In exam answers, state **the definition**, then **one balanced equation**.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the reactants are alkanes, alkenes or sugars.
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Addition:** an unsaturated compound adds a small molecule across its double bond to form one saturated product, $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}} + \mathrm{Br_{2}} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}Br_{2}}$ (bromine water is decolourised). **Substitution:** a hydrogen atom of an alkane is replaced by another atom, in sunlight, $\mathrm{CH_{4}} + \mathrm{Cl_{2}} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_{3}Cl} + \mathrm{HCl}$. **Addition polymerisation:** many small unsaturated molecules (monomers) join to form one very long molecule (a polymer) and nothing else is formed, for example $n\,\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} \rightarrow \left[\mathrm{CH_2 - CH_2}\right]_n$ (ethene to poly(ethene)). **Fermentation:** glucose is changed by enzymes in yeast, $\mathrm{C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH} + 2\mathrm{CO_{2}}$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question mentions heat given out or a double arrow.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Exothermic reactions (combustion, neutralisation, respiration) release heat and the temperature rises. Endothermic reactions (thermal decomposition) take in heat. A **reversible reaction** can go in both directions and uses the sign $\rightleftharpoons$, for example the Haber process $\mathrm{N_{2}} + 3\mathrm{H_{2}} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH_{3}}$.

variantes.nom: Acids with metals, oxides and carbonates
variantes.quand_utiliser: When an acid is a reactant.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Acid + metal: $\mathrm{Zn} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{ZnCl_{2}} + \mathrm{H_{2}}$ (displacement of hydrogen). Acid + metal oxide (a base): $\mathrm{CuO} + \mathrm{H_{2}SO_{4}} \rightarrow \mathrm{CuSO_{4}} + \mathrm{H_{2}O}$ (neutralisation). Acid + carbonate: $\mathrm{CaCO_{3}} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaCl_{2}} + \mathrm{H_{2}O} + \mathrm{CO_{2}}$ (carbon dioxide bubbles).

sections.enonce_markdown:
Name the type of each reaction and give one observation or reason.

A: $\mathrm{CuCO_{3}} \rightarrow \mathrm{CuO} + \mathrm{CO_{2}}$

B: $\mathrm{Mg} + \mathrm{CuSO_{4}} \rightarrow \mathrm{MgSO_{4}} + \mathrm{Cu}$

C: $\mathrm{Pb(NO_{3})_{2}} + 2\mathrm{KI} \rightarrow \mathrm{PbI_{2}} + 2\mathrm{KNO_{3}}$

D: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}} + \mathrm{H_{2}} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_{2}H_{6}}$

E: $2\mathrm{Na} + \mathrm{Cl_{2}} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaCl}$

etapes.justification: One reactant breaks into two products when heated.
etapes.resultat_markdown: **Thermal decomposition**: green solid turns black and carbon dioxide is released.

etapes.justification: An element reacts with a compound and the element takes the place of another element in the compound.
etapes.resultat_markdown: **Displacement**: magnesium is more reactive than copper; the blue colour fades and copper forms.

etapes.justification: Two compounds in solution exchange partners.
etapes.resultat_markdown: **Double decomposition (precipitation)**: a yellow precipitate of lead(II) iodide forms.

etapes.justification: An alkene adds a small molecule across its double bond and one saturated product forms.
Two elements join to give one compound.
etapes.resultat_markdown: **Combination**. It is also a redox reaction because sodium loses electrons and chlorine gains them.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The pattern of reactants and products identifies the type: A decomposition, B displacement, C precipitation, D addition and E combination (and redox).

items.erreur_markdown: "Zn + CuSO4 is a double decomposition reaction."
items.pourquoi_faux: In double decomposition, two compounds exchange partners. Here an element replaces another element in a compound.
items.correction_markdown: This is displacement: zinc displaces copper from copper(II) sulphate.

items.pourquoi_faux: An acid reacting with a base produces a salt as well as water.

items.erreur_markdown: "Addition polymerisation of ethene gives poly(ethene) and water."
items.pourquoi_faux: Water is a by-product of condensation polymerisation. In addition polymerisation, the monomer molecules join and nothing else is formed.
items.correction_markdown: Only the polymer forms, so the mass of the polymer equals the mass of the monomer used.

items.pourquoi_faux: Decomposition can also be caused by electricity (electrolysis) or by light.
items.correction_markdown: Electrolysis of water: $2\mathrm{H_{2}O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{H_{2}} + \mathrm{O_{2}}$. Heat is needed only in *thermal* decomposition.

items.erreur_markdown: "A reaction can belong to only one type."
items.pourquoi_faux: Types overlap. Burning magnesium combines two elements, burns in oxygen and transfers electrons.
items.correction_markdown: $2\mathrm{Mg} + \mathrm{O_{2}} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MgO}$ is a combination, a combustion and a redox reaction.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the type of reaction in each case. (a) Zinc is added to copper(II) sulphate solution. (b) Hydrochloric acid is added to sodium hydroxide solution. (c) Marble ($\mathrm{CaCO_{3}}$) is heated strongly. (d) Silver nitrate solution is added to sodium chloride solution and a white solid forms. (e) Iron filings and sulphur powder are heated together and form iron(II) sulphide, $\mathrm{Fe} + \mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{FeS}$.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Displacement**. (b) **Neutralisation**. (c) **Thermal decomposition**. (d) **Double decomposition (precipitation)**; the white solid is silver chloride. (e) **Combination** (and it is also redox).

items.enonce_markdown: Write a balanced equation for each of the following and name the type of reaction. (a) Sulphuric acid with potassium hydroxide solution. (b) Magnesium with dilute hydrochloric acid. (c) Barium chloride solution with sodium sulphate solution. (d) Ethene gas with bromine, $\mathrm{Br_2}$.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $\mathrm{H_{2}SO_{4}} + 2\mathrm{KOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{K_{2}SO_{4}} + 2\mathrm{H_{2}O}$ **neutralisation**.

(b) $\mathrm{Mg} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{MgCl_{2}} + \mathrm{H_{2}}$ **displacement** (of hydrogen), also redox.

(c) $\mathrm{BaCl_{2}} + \mathrm{Na_{2}SO_{4}} \rightarrow \mathrm{BaSO_{4}} + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ **double decomposition (precipitation)**; a white precipitate of barium sulphate forms.

(d) $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}} + \mathrm{Br_{2}} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}Br_{2}}$ **addition**; brown bromine is decolourised.

items.enonce_markdown: Poly(ethene) is made from ethene, $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$, by addition polymerisation. (a) Define addition polymerisation and explain why ethene can undergo it. (b) A sample of poly(ethene) has a relative molecular mass of $28\,000$. How many ethene molecules joined to form one molecule of the polymer? (c) What mass of poly(ethene) is formed from 5.6 kg of ethene, if all of it reacts? (d) Methane reacts with chlorine in sunlight: $\mathrm{CH_{4}} + \mathrm{Cl_{2}} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_{3}Cl} + \mathrm{HCl}$. Name this type of reaction and say how it differs from the reaction of ethene with bromine.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Addition polymerisation is the joining of many small unsaturated molecules (monomers) to make one very long molecule (a polymer) with no other product. Ethene has a carbon-carbon double bond that can open to link with other molecules.

(b) $M_r(\mathrm{C_2H_4}) = 28$. Number of molecules $= \dfrac{28\,000}{28} = $ **$1\,000$**.

(c) No other product forms, so the mass of polymer equals the mass of ethene: **5.6 kg**.

(d) It is a **substitution** reaction, in which a hydrogen atom of methane is replaced by a chlorine atom and two products form. In the addition reaction of ethene with bromine the two bromine atoms add across the double bond and only **one** product forms.

items_markdown: Identify the type from the pattern: combination (many to one), decomposition (one to many), displacement (element replaces element), precipitation (two solutions give an insoluble solid), neutralisation (acid + base gives salt + water).
Decomposition can be caused by heat (thermal), electricity (electrolysis) or light.
Addition reactions of alkenes give one saturated product; substitution reactions of alkanes replace a hydrogen atom.
In addition polymerisation, many monomer molecules form a polymer and nothing else.
Redox, exothermic and endothermic describe electron transfer and energy, and can apply to reactions of other types.
